sec: PTH adverse effects, receptors, sigmoid rule and CaSR mutations · p873

items.q: Adverse effects of PTH on the CVS include:
items.exp: CVS adverse effects: medial calcification, atherosclerosis, HTN. (Book p873)

items.q: The PTH receptor type on which PTHrP also acts, mediating paraneoplastic hypercalcaemia (squamous cell carcinoma of head & neck, lung), is:
items.exp: Type 1 receptor: PTHrp also acts here → paraneoplastic role (SCC head & neck, lung). (Book p873)

items.q: ‘A fall in ionised calcium is the MORE sensitive stimulus, inhibiting CaSR and raising PTH; a rise activates CaSR and lowers PTH.’
opts: False — CaSR is in the kidney only
True, but only with high phosphate
items.exp: Sigmoid rule: ↑Ca2+ activates CaSR → ↓PTH; ↓Ca2+ (more sensitive) inhibits CaSR → ↑PTH. (Book p873)

items.q: The most important regulator of PTH is:
items.exp: Ionised Ca2+ is the most important regulator; basal PTH secretion is always present. (Book p873)
Deficiency of P impairs PTH release. (Book p873)

items.q: Match CaSR mutation — 1) Loss of function  2) Gain of function … A) Bartter syndrome type 5  B) Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia
items.exp: CaSR loss-of-function → familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia; gain-of-function → Bartter syndrome type 5. (Book p873)

items.q: Senile osteoporosis arises because mesenchymal stem cells differentiate into:
items.exp: Senile osteoporosis: mesenchymal stem cells → adipocyte instead of osteoblast. (Book p873)

items.q: ___ helps in Ca2+ reabsorption from the kidney.
items.exp: Claudin 16 helps in Ca2+ reabsorption from kidney. (Book p873)
